newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to ship waste to N.Korea in July - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to ship waste to N.Korea in July - paper.

text.p: Taiwan is expected to ship an initial batch of nuclear waste to North Korea in July despite fierce protests from South Korea, local press reported on Tuesday.

Three North Korean officials arrived in Taipei on Tuesday and would submit a detailed plan to state-owned Taiwan Power Company for the waste shipment to be disposed in the communist country, the United Evening News said.
The newspaper, quoting unnamed sources, said North Korea hoped that the first batch of low-radiation nuclear waste could be shipped to Pyongyang by July.

Taipower signed a contract with Pyongyang in January for the disposal in North Korea of up to 200,000 barrels of contaminated clothing, gloves and helmets discarded from Taiwan's three nuclear power plants.
South Korea, bitter rival of the Stalinist North Korea, has sharply protested the move, citing environmental and health hazards, and sought international support to stop the shipment.
The newspaper said Taipower would review the North Korea shipment plan carefully before sending it to Taipei's Atomic Energy Council for final approval.
Taipower officials were tight-lipped over the report. One executive told Reuters his company was ready to begin shipping as soon as North Korea submits a final disposal plan.

Taipower has declined to comment on press reports that it would pay Pyongyang US$1,150 per barrel to store the waste, which would make the deal worth up to US$230 million -- money desperately needed by the impoverished country.
Yang Chih-fang, director of North Korea's unofficial representative office in Taipei, also declined to comment on the report.
Pyongyang only has diplomatic relations with China which considers Taiwan a renegade province.
